html:
A great medieval merchant guild of south India, named after its home town of Ayyavole, today's Aihole in Karnataka. It flourished from about the 9th to the 13th century.

The "Five Hundred" was a title, not a head count. The guild was a large body of traders with its own banner, rules, armed guards and a praise poem about its members' virtues. It dealt in spices, gems, horses, cloth and perfumes, and worked with local merchant groups in the towns it served.

It grew strongest under the Chola Empire, whose navy reached across the Bay of Bengal in the raid on Srivijaya of 1025. Inscriptions left by the guild or its partners have been found in Sri Lanka, Burma, Thailand and at Barus in Sumatra. It was one of the networks that made the Indian Ocean trade of those centuries run, much like the merchant guilds of Europe later.
